entries.subject: dom: avoid quadratic copying when collecting wildcard JSONPath matches (#2901)
entries.message:
dom: avoid quadratic copying when collecting wildcard JSONPath matches (#2901)

process_json_path_of_child_elements reserved exactly size() + n before
appending each child's matches. An exact reserve disables the vector's
geometric growth, so every child reallocated and copied everything
collected so far: O(n^2) in the number of matches. insert() alone
grows geometrically.

$[*][*] over a 16000 x 50 array (800000 matches): 6.4 s -> 6 ms.

entries.subject: Detect reentrant array access during iteration in development checks (#2886)
entries.message:
Detect reentrant array access during iteration in development checks (#2886)

Mirror the object locking from #2809 for ondemand::array. While an
array_iterator from array::begin() is alive, calling at(), count_elements(),
is_empty(), reset() or begin() on the same array returns
OUT_OF_ORDER_ITERATION under SIMDJSON_DEVELOPMENT_CHECKS.

raw_json() is left unguarded, unlike the object side, because
ondemand_tostring_tests serializes an array while its iterator is still
alive and expects that to work.

value::begin() and document::begin() iterate a temporary array from
get_array(), so a locking iterator there would outlive the array and
unlock it after it is gone (ASan reports stack-use-after-scope in
array::set_locked). Those two use a non-locking begin_unlocked() instead.

Related to #2314.

* Add single 8-bit-window fast path to key_selector

  Introduce a compile-time discriminator that tells a small key set apart by
  reading a single, possibly byte-unaligned 8-bit window of the key bytes. When
  such a window exists, compute_window builds a 256-entry table mapping the
  window value straight to a candidate key, which match_window_candidate then
  confirms with a length-free byte comparison and a closing-quote check;
  unaligned windows separate sets that no aligned byte can (e.g. the
  partial_tweets keys), while simpler cases fall out as the shift==0 special
  case. This replaces the hash computation and SIMD length scan with a two-byte
  load, a shift, a mask, and a table lookup on the hot path, which measurably
  speeds up object field matching on representative inputs such as the
  partial_tweets benchmark where every key set qualifies for a window. The path
  is detected via consteval and selected with if constexpr, so the hash path is
  compiled out for key sets that qualify and the window path is compiled out for
  those that do not. object::for_each now branches on Selector::window.ok to take
  the length-free field_key path (no backward scan, mirroring the ordered
  find_field) and feed match_raw(raw_json_string) when a window selector is in
  use, falling back to the length-aware hash path otherwise. Add tests covering
  single-byte discriminators ("id"/"screen_name"), quote-terminated prefixes
  ("jo"/"joe"), and the unaligned partial_tweets window, including misses that
  share a prefix or discriminating byte.

* Fix MSVC build: use std::memcpy instead of __builtin_memcpy in key_selector

MSVC does not provide __builtin_memcpy, causing C3861 in read_window().
std::memcpy (via <cstring>) is the portable unaligned little-endian load and
is equally optimized; read_window is a runtime (non-constexpr) helper so this

entries.subject: builder: restore `pos + n <= cap` in writer::ensure (fixes citm serialization regression) (#2874)
entries.message:
builder: restore `pos + n <= cap` in writer::ensure (fixes citm serialization regression) (#2874)

Commit a16e5128 ("pendantic guard") rewrote the hot capacity check in
writer::ensure() from `pos + n <= cap` to `n <= cap - pos` to rule out
a wrap of `pos + n` on 32-bit targets. That one-line change costs
14-20% of serialization throughput on citm_catalog.json under GCC 16
(arm64): the `cap - pos` remainder is an extra live value across the
fully inlined serializer, and GCC cannot canonicalize between the two
forms because they differ under wrap. The inlined citm append() grew
from 129KB to 145KB with ~11% more loads/stores.

Restore `pos + n <= cap` and instead keep the wrap protection where
the only data-dependent `n` originates: the string and map-key atoms
now check `size() > (SIZE_MAX - 2 - pos) / 6` (resp. `- 3 - pos`),
which proves `pos + 2 + 6*size` cannot wrap. All other ensure()
callers pass constexpr key/enum lengths. The guard branches were
measured as free.

Interleaved max-of-best, GCC 16.1, Release, static reflection:

  citm/reuse_buffer          9058 -> 10866 MB/s  (+20%)
  citm/static_reflection     8182 ->  9476 MB/s  (+16%)
  citm/to                    7323 ->  8331 MB/s  (+14%)
  citm/to_reuse              7309 ->  8337 MB/s  (+14%)
  twitter (all four)         within +/-2% (noise)

entries.subject: perf: stage2: decode adjacent Unicode escapes without rescanning (#2882)
entries.message:
perf: stage2: decode adjacent Unicode escapes without rescanning (#2882)

Escaped Unicode strings can contain consecutive \uXXXX sequences. After
  decoding the first escape, decode the remaining adjacent escapes directly
  instead of returning to the quote-and-backslash scanner between code points.

  This avoids repeated SIMD scans and mask reduction for adjacent Unicode
  escapes. Because it is implemented in generic Stage 2 code, the optimization
  can benefit adjacent-Unicode workloads across all architectures.

  Parsing resumes through the existing scanner as soon as the adjacent run
  ends, leaving the normal string-scanning path unchanged.

Improve build times for debug builds (#1859)

* Rename simdjson_really_inline -> simdjson_inline

I want to change the simdjson_really_inline macro to sometimes not force
inlining. After that upcoming change, the name simdjson_really_inline
will no longer makes sense.

Rename simdjson_really_inline to simdjson_inline. This patch should not
change semantics; simdjson_inline still forces inlining as before.

Some functions still need to be really inlined for ABI reasons.
(GCC's -Wpsabi complains otherwise.) Leave those functions marked as
simdjson_really_inline.

* Improve build times for debug builds

simdjson_inline is used for most simdjson functions. It forces inlining.
In unoptimized/debug builds, this can lead to a lot of machine code
being generated (especially with Address Sanitizer), causing slow
compilation.

Change simdjson_inline to force inlining only for optimized builds.

Sometimes, the programmer might want a slightly-optimized build and want
fast compilation (e.g. GCC's -Og mode). Allow simdjson users to define
the simdjson_inline macro themselves (e.g. on the command line:
-Dsimdjson_inline=inline) in cases where the default behavior is
undesired.

This patch reduced build times by over 75% for ondemand_object_tests.cpp
with GCC 9.4.0 and CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug on my AMD 5950X:

Before: 6.885 6.683 6.971 6.957 6.949 seconds (5 samples)
After:  1.492 1.551 1.494 1.490 1.531 seconds (5 samples)

entries.subject: CI: test each pull request once, trim Windows jobs; regenerate the single header for 5.0.2 (#2902)
entries.message:
CI: test each pull request once, trim Windows jobs; regenerate the single header for 5.0.2 (#2902)

* CI: test each pull request once, cancel superseded runs, trim Windows jobs

- Workflows that ran on every push and every pull request now run on
  pushes to master and on pull requests only. A branch of this repository
  with an open pull request was tested twice. All of them can also be run
  by hand (workflow_dispatch).
- Add a concurrency group to every workflow: a new push to a pull request
  cancels its previous run. Pushes to master and scheduled runs are never
  cancelled.
- LoongArch64, Emscripten and Ubuntu 22.04 clang 13/14 now run on master
  only (or by hand).
- Windows: 30 jobs down to 19. vs18-clang-ci-cxx20.yml was an exact copy
  of vs18-clang-ci.yml (same name, no C++20 flag); it is now a single
  ClangCL C++20 build. RelWithDebInfo jobs are dropped, as are a few
  redundant shared/static and NaN/Inf combinations.

* Regenerate the single header for 5.0.2 (include #2901)

* document_stream: make truncated_bytes() correct for json_sequence and comma_delimited

The json_sequence and comma_delimited stage-1 filters drop RS markers and
root-level commas by compacting structural_indexes in place. That left a stale
index in the slot past the compacted end, where stage 1 had stored the input
length, and the final batch copies that slot into the bookkeeping that
truncated_bytes() reads. Complete streams therefore reported spurious
truncated bytes: e.g. 2 for the comma-delimited input `1,2,3`, or 3 for the
json_sequence input `\x1e{"a":1}\n\x1e[2]\n`.

Restore the sentinel after compaction in both filters (shared by every kernel,
including fallback). Truncated tails are still reported: `{"a":1},{"b":`
yields 5. The extra store has no measurable cost (json_sequence and
comma_delimited parse_many throughput within noise on Apple M4 and on Xeon
Gold 6548N).

Update the iterate_many/parse_many docs and the document_stream headers: the
value is now meaningful in every format, under the same conditions as
before (iterate to the end, no document error). Add a regression test and
regenerate the single header.

* Faster static-reflection serialization and deserialization

Serialization (builder):
- Compute an upper bound on the output size with reflection, reserve it once,
  then write through an unchecked writer (no capacity check per write).
- to_json(z, std::string&) writes straight into the string with
  resize_and_overwrite instead of copying out of a string_builder.
- Copy keys as padded 16-byte blocks; force write_string_escaped inline and
  scan 32 bytes at a time with AVX2.
- Replace the integer writer with jeaiii's algorithm (two 200-byte tables).

Deserialization:
- Collect vector elements in a per-thread scratch vector, then move them into
  an exactly reserved vector: one allocation instead of repeated regrowth.
- Parse integers eight digits at a time when they have at least eight digits.

* Fix review findings: truncated_bytes() on an unclosed string, 32-bit bound overflow, bad_alloc in the vector path

- json_sequence and comma_delimited: the stage-1 filters restored len as the
  EOF sentinel, but after a discarded unclosed string stage 1 had planted the
  string's start there, so truncated_bytes() returned 0. Keep the planted value.
- The size bound (a sum of 6 * string sizes) can overflow a 32-bit size_t, and
  the unchecked writer would then overrun the buffer: use it on 64-bit only.
- Reserve before marking the scratch-vector collection complete, so that a
  bad_alloc from reserve still leaves the parsed elements in out.

* Fix CI: GCC 13 stringop-overflow in string_builder::append(double), kernel-dependent test

- Restore the original body of string_builder::append(double): computing the
  position from the pointer returned by write_double() made GCC 13.3 (Ubuntu
  24.04, SIMDJSON_ENABLE_NAN_INF=ON) report a bogus out-of-bounds write.
  write_double() is now used only by the unchecked reflection writer.
- In the json_sequence truncated_bytes() test, put a space before the unclosed
  string: whether a quote right after an RS is a structural depends on the
  SIMD kernel, which changed the expected count (4 or 5) from one to the next.

* Regenerate the single header

* dom::parse_many: honor number_as_string(), copy only the number for root numbers

- document_stream::start() now passes number_as_string() to the parser
  implementation, as parse() does: on a fresh parser, parse_many() reported
  BIGINT_ERROR for integers that do not fit in 64 bits.
- visit_root_number made its space-padded copy from the number to the end of
  the input, which in a stream is the rest of the batch: a stream of bare
  numbers was hundreds of times slower. Copy up to the next structural only.

* Regenerate the single header

entries.message:
Require POWER8 vector support for ppc64 SIMD code (#2851)

The ppc64 kernel and the string builder SIMD path use VSX and POWER8
builtins (vec_vsx_ld, vec_vbpermq, 64-bit __vector types), but are
enabled whenever AltiVec is available. On targets whose baseline CPU
predates VSX (e.g. FreeBSD/powerpc64, which targets the 970), this
breaks the build:

error: use of 'long long' with '__vector' requires VSX support (available on POWER7 or later) to be enabled
error: use of undeclared identifier 'vec_vbpermq'

Gate both on __POWER8_VECTOR__ so such targets use the fallback paths,
while ppc64le (POWER8 baseline) and builds with -mcpu=power8 or newer
are unaffected.

entries.subject: DOM without padding (experimental) (#2775)
entries.message:
DOM without padding (experimental) (#2775)

* Add dom::parser::parse_unpadded for zero-copy parsing of unpadded input

Adds a DOM API that parses JSON directly from a buffer with no trailing
SIMDJSON_PADDING, without copying it into a padded buffer (unlike
parse(buf, len, realloc_if_needed=true)).

Only string parsing over-reads for unpadded input: stage 1 already tail-copies
its last block, non-root numbers/atoms are followed by an in-buffer structural
char, root numbers copy, and root atoms use the remaining_len-aware validators.
So the change is minimal and isolated:

- stringparsing.h: parse_string_safe(), which runs the normal parse_string fast
  loop while >= SIMDJSON_PADDING bytes from the end, then finishes the final
  <64 bytes from a space-padded scratch via the unchanged parse_string (keeps
  the delicate escape/Unicode handling in one proven place).
- internal::dom_parser_implementation: a _unpadded flag (default false).
- tape_builder is split into tape_builder_impl<bool UNPADDED> (visit_string uses
  `if constexpr (UNPADDED)`) and a thin tape_builder whose parse_document picks
  the instantiation ONCE per document from the flag. The padded path therefore
  has NO per-string branch or flag load: it is byte-for-byte the same codegen as
  before (verified: 360.06 vs 360.06 instructions/block on twitter.json, vs
  +5.5/block for a runtime flag). walk_document and json_iterator are untouched.
- dom::parser: parse_unpadded / parse_into_document_unpadded public API.

New test tests/dom/unpadded_tests.cpp parses from exact-size heap buffers so any
read past buf+len is caught under AddressSanitizer; it sweeps the closing-quote
across the padding boundary, escapes/surrogates at the end, root primitives,
degenerate inputs, and real files.

entries.subject: Fix just_ascii test failure: replace em dashes with ASCII (#2821)
entries.message:
Fix just_ascii test failure: replace em dashes with ASCII (#2821)

The just_ascii test has been failing on master (and consequently on every
open PR) because several headers contain U+2014 EM DASH in comments. Those
headers are amalgamated into singleheader/simdjson.cpp, which the test does
scan, so the failure surfaced there:

    The following files contain non-ASCII characters:
    singleheader/simdjson.cpp: C source, Unicode text, UTF-8 text

Replace every em dash with an ASCII "--" in the eight affected source files
and in the checked-in amalgamation.

Also fix a find(1) operator-precedence bug that let this go unnoticed. In

    find ... -path X -prune -name '*.h' -o -name '*.cpp' -type f -exec file {} \;

-o binds looser than the implicit -a, so the expression grouped as

    ( -path X -a -prune -a -name '*.h' ) -o ( -name '*.cpp' -a -type f -a -exec ... )

meaning only .cpp files were ever passed to file(1), and the prune branch
never matched a directory. Headers could carry non-ASCII indefinitely and
were only caught indirectly, via the amalgamated .cpp. Parenthesizing the
name tests restores the intent: the scan now covers 530 files instead of
150, and the prune actually prunes.

entries.subject: perf: SIMD string escaping and batch integer formatting optimizations (#2605)
entries.message:
perf: SIMD string escaping and batch integer formatting optimizations (#2605)

* perf(serialization): SIMD-accelerated string escape position finding

Profiling revealed that string serialization was performing redundant
scanning: first calling fast_needs_escaping() (SIMD scan to check IF
escape needed), then find_next_json_quotable_character() (scalar
byte-by-byte scan to find WHERE).

Profile data from Twitter benchmark showed:
- 54.76% time in atom<std::string> (string serialization)
- 24.85% time in find_next_json_quotable_character (scalar position finding)

This optimization unifies both operations into a single SIMD pass that
directly locates the first quotable character position:

- NEON (ARM64): Uses vceqq_u8/vcltq_u8 for character detection, then
  extracts position via __builtin_ctzll on 64-bit vector lanes
- SSE2 (x86-64): Uses _mm_cmpeq_epi8/_mm_subs_epu8 for detection, then
  _mm_movemask_epi8 + __builtin_ctz for position extraction

The write_string_escaped function now uses the position finder directly,
eliminating the separate fast_needs_escaping check.

Benchmark results (ARM64, Apple Silicon via Docker with p2996 clang):
- Twitter (string-heavy): 4330 -> 5723 MB/s (+32%)
- CITM (numeric-heavy): ~neutral (expected, few strings)

* perf(serialization): batch integer formatting with 4-digit processing

Profiling with perf annotate revealed that the integer-to-string
conversion loop was a significant hotspot in numeric-heavy workloads.
The original implementation processed 2 digits per iteration:

    while (pv >= 100) {
        memcpy(write_pointer - 1, &decimal_table[(pv % 100) * 2], 2);
        write_pointer -= 2;
        pv /= 100;
    }

Profile data from CITM benchmark showed:
- 31.20% time in atom<unsigned long> (integer formatting)
- 39.07% of integer formatting time in the 2-byte store instruction
  (sturh on ARM64)
- CITM integers average 8.8 digits, meaning 4+ store operations per number

This optimization processes 4 digits per iteration, reducing both store
operations and division count by approximately half for large numbers:

    while (pv >= 10000) {
        q = pv / 10000;
        r = pv % 10000;
        r_hi = r / 100;  // High 2 digits
        r_lo = r % 100;  // Low 2 digits
        memcpy(write_pointer - 1, &decimal_table[r_lo * 2], 2);
        memcpy(write_pointer - 3, &decimal_table[r_hi * 2], 2);
        write_pointer -= 4;
        pv = q;
    }

The division by 10000 compiles to an efficient multiply-high instruction
(umulh on ARM64). Applied to both unsigned and signed integer paths.

Benchmark results (ARM64, Apple Silicon via Docker with p2996 clang):
- Twitter: ~neutral (few integers)
- CITM (numeric-heavy): 2912 -> 3086 MB/s (+6%)

* fix(build): add MSVC compatibility for bit manipulation intrinsics

MSVC does not have __builtin_ctz/__builtin_ctzll. Use _BitScanForward
and _BitScanForward64 from <intrin.h> on MSVC instead.

This fixes the build on all Windows configurations (x64, ARM64, Win32).

* refactor: clean up comments to be implementation-focused

Remove references to specific benchmarks and previous implementations
from code comments. Comments now describe what the code does rather
than historical context.

fix: prevent parse_unpadded 1-byte OOB on truncated nested JSON (#2817)

* fix: prevent parse_unpadded 1-byte OOB on truncated nested JSON

Stage 1 plants a sentinel structural index equal to `len` after the last
real structural. On the padded path, reading buf[len] is safe. With
parse_unpadded, that read is a heap-buffer-overflow when stage2's
array_continue/object_continue advances past the end of an incomplete
nested document (e.g. "[[]", "{\"a\":{}").

Guard peek()/advance() so unpadded input returns a static dummy byte
instead of buf[len]; walk_document then reports TAPE_ERROR as usual.

Add truncated_nested_containers regression tests for the three cases
from #2815 (exact-size buffers; ASAN-sensitive).

Fixes #2815

The runtime _unpadded flag is still set once per parse_unpadded call, but
tape_builder::parse_document already branches on it to choose
tape_builder_impl<true/false>. Thread the same compile-time UNPADDED
parameter through walk_document, peek, and advance so the padded stage2
path no longer loads _unpadded or bounds-checks on every token.

Uses SIMDJSON_IF_CONSTEXPR so C++17+ eliminates the unpadded branch from
the padded instantiation entirely.

runtime check there was misleading and not the real fix. The library

entries.subject: Faster write_string_escaped: single-pass block escaping (SSE2, NEON) (#2795)
entries.message:
Faster write_string_escaped: single-pass block escaping (SSE2, NEON) (#2795)

* Faster write_string_escaped: single-pass block escaping (SSE2 and NEON)

write_string_escaped scanned the input for the next quotable character and
then copied the run, so every byte was visited twice, and the scan fell back
to a byte-at-a-time table lookup for anything shorter than a SIMD block.
Since the median JSON string is short (11 bytes in twitter.json, 8 in
citm_catalog.json), most strings never reached the vector path at all.

Instead, consume the input in 16-byte blocks and copy a block with a single
unaligned SIMD store when it holds nothing to escape, which makes one pass
over the data. Blocks that do need escaping are fixed up from the escape
mask, so whole runs between escapes are memcpy'd rather than rescanned.

The tail (fewer than 16 bytes) is covered by overlapping loads that stay
entirely inside the input -- the last 16 bytes when the string is at least
that long, otherwise two overlapping 8-byte or 4-byte loads. Nothing reads
past the end of the string, so this is clean under sanitizers and safe for
inputs ending at a page boundary. Strings shorter than 4 bytes stay scalar.

Getting the comparison result out of the vector register file is the step
that decides whether any of this pays off, so each instruction set tests
"does this block need escaping?" its own cheapest way: pmovmskb on SSE2, and
on NEON a shift-and-narrow compared as a double, which keeps the answer in
the FP register file. Other instruction sets keep the existing
scan-then-copy path.

Serialization benchmarks on a Xeon Gold 6548N with GCC 16, best of three
interleaved rounds:

                        twitter    citm_catalog
    static_reflection    +17.8%          +4.8%
    reuse_buffer         +20.8%          +5.9%
    to                   +14.1%          +8.7%
    to_reuse             +14.4%          +8.5%

Throughput of write_string_escaped alone, over every string in each file:

    Xeon Gold 6548N   twitter 1.86x   citm 2.13x
    Apple M4 Max      twitter 2.43x   citm 2.83x

NEON still trails the old path for strings of 128 bytes and up, where a
well-tuned memcpy beats copying 16 bytes at a time. Sharing one zero test
across four blocks recovers that, but costs about half the win on the short
strings that dominate real documents, so it is not done here.

Verified against a reference escaper with 12060 randomized cases per
architecture, under ASan+UBSan, and with the full test suite.

* Escape runs with copy_lt16 and keep escape_block out of line

The runs of safe bytes between escapes are always shorter than a block,
but memcpy does not know that: both GCC and clang emit a call for these
variable-length copies, one per escape. copy_lt16 covers the same range
with overlapping loads and stores and no call, and folding the leading
run into the loop removes the -1/+1 offsets that the separate head copy
needed.

Inlining that into escape_block, however, costs registers in the block
loop that runs for every 16 bytes of input, and the compiler starts
hoisting work into the prologue -- citm_catalog, where no string
contains a quotable character and escape_block never runs, still paid
for it. escape_block only runs for blocks that need escaping, so mark
it simdjson_never_inline and let the hot loop keep its registers.

Both changes are needed: separately each one regresses some input, and
neither subsumes the other.

Escaping every string of the corpus through string_builder, best of six
interleaved rounds, against the previous commit:

                          twitter   citm_catalog   escaped strings only
  M4 Max, clang            +18.4%        +39.4%                 +49.4%
  Xeon 6548N, GCC 14       +14.2%        +14.8%                 +21.2%
  Xeon 6548N, clang 21      +6.7%         +4.9%                 +34.2%

The last column is the 312 twitter.json strings that actually contain a
quotable character; that case was slower than before this branch, and
is now faster.

Credit to @fior512, who proposed the loop restructuring in review.

* Give simdjson_never_inline inline linkage under Visual Studio

escape_block is a header function marked simdjson_never_inline. On GCC
and Clang that macro expands to 'inline __attribute__((noinline))', but
under Visual Studio it expanded to '__declspec(noinline)' alone, which
says nothing about linkage. The function therefore got external linkage
and was emitted in every translation unit including simdjson.h, so the
multiple_include test failed to link:

  mylib.lib(mylib.obj) : error LNK2005:
  "char * __cdecl simdjson::fallback::builder::escape_block(...)"
  already defined in main.obj

The two definitions of the macro were meant to be equivalent; spell out
the 'inline' on the Visual Studio side. __forceinline, used just above
for simdjson_really_inline, already implies it, which is why this was
the only one missing.

Checked by reproducing the exact failure on Clang with the 'inline'
removed from the GCC/Clang definition (same symbol, same error), and by
confirming with -fms-extensions that 'inline __declspec(noinline)'
links across two translation units and still leaves the function out of
line at its call sites.

entries.subject: Detect C++26 static reflection instead of requiring a build flag (#2798)
entries.message:
Detect C++26 static reflection instead of requiring a build flag (#2798)

* Detect C++26 static reflection instead of requiring a build flag

SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION defaulted to 0 in the headers, so the
reflection-based APIs were reachable only by defining the macro by hand
or by configuring the CMake option. Someone who dropped simdjson.h and
simdjson.cpp into their project and compiled with a C++26 compiler --
the way most people consume simdjson -- got nothing.

Detect the feature set instead. Reflection needs more than the
reflection operator, so the check covers all of what the code uses that
has a feature-test macro:

  P2996 reflection (^^, splicers, <meta>)  __cpp_impl_reflection,
                                           __cpp_lib_reflection
  P1306 expansion statements               __cpp_expansion_statements
  P3491 define_static_string/_array        __cpp_lib_define_static

Two more features we use, annotations (P3394) and consteval blocks
(P3289), have no feature-test macro of their own; GCC 16 implements
both and does not advertise either. Every implementation that provides
the four macros above also provides those two, and the comment in
compiler_check.h records that assumption. SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION
remains overridable, so a compiler that gets this wrong in either
direction can still be pinned.

Being in C++26 mode is not by itself enough: compilers ask you to opt
into reflection, and GCC 16 only defines __cpp_impl_reflection under
-freflection. So detection turns on precisely when the user asked their
compiler for reflection, which is the intended trigger.

The CMake variable becomes AUTO (new default) / ON / OFF. AUTO leaves
the language mode alone and lets the headers decide; ON keeps the old
behaviour of adding -std=c++26 -freflection and forcing the macro; OFF
now forces the macro to 0 rather than merely not setting it. The
resolved answer is exposed internally as
SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION_ENABLED, which is what the test and
benchmark directories now gate on -- "AUTO" is a true-ish string to
if(), so they could not keep testing the user-facing variable.

Also stop overwriting a CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD the user set explicitly, and
fix SIMDJSON_CPLUSPLUS26, whose 202402L threshold no compiler reaches
(GCC 16 and Clang 21 both report 202400L in C++26 mode).

tests/reflection_autodetect_tests.cpp checks that the headers and the
build system agree on the detected value and that the matching API
works; a new gcc16 CI job compiles it against the amalgamation with and
without -freflection, so the single-header promise is covered without a
build system.

Verified with GCC 16.1 (x86-64 and arm64 containers):
  - single header + -std=c++26 -freflection: reflection on, round-trip
    through rename/skip annotations works, no macro and no CMake
  - a libsimdjson.a built with plain defaults still serves a C++26
    consumer that uses reflection
  - -std=c++26 without -freflection, and C++11/17/20: reflection off,
    ordinary API unaffected
  - developer mode, reflection forced ON: 137/137 ctest
  - developer mode, AUTO with no C++26: 131/131 ctest
  - developer mode, forced OFF: 130/130 ctest
  - Apple clang, AUTO: 119/119 ctest, reflection correctly not detected

* Rename the reflection CMake setting to SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION_MODE

Reusing SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION for a three-valued setting broke the
performance check. The name used to be a boolean, and CMake's if() treats
every string other than a short list (empty, 0, OFF, NO, FALSE, N, IGNORE,
NOTFOUND, *-NOTFOUND) as true -- AUTO included.

That matters because cmake/simdjson-user-cmakecache.cmake copies every
SIMDJSON_* cache entry into the reference build that
benchmark/dom/checkperf.cmake configures against master. Master still writes
`if(SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION)` and, seeing the string AUTO, added
-std=c++26 -freflection to a GCC 13 build:

    c++: error: unrecognized command-line option '-freflection'
    c++: error: unrecognized command-line option '-std=c++26'

Any project that vendors an older simdjson, or that still tests the variable
the documented way, would have hit the same thing. So put the three-valued
setting under a new name and leave the old one boolean. The old spelling is
still accepted, mapped to ON/OFF, with a deprecation message.

The preprocessor macro SIMDJSON_STATIC_REFLECTION keeps its name and meaning;
only the CMake variable moved.

Also initialize `value` in reflection_autodetect_tests.cpp. GCC cannot see
that get() leaves it untouched exactly on the path that returns early, so
-Wmaybe-uninitialized fired and the no-exceptions and no-threads builds
compile with -Werror.

Checked by handing the filtered user cache to a master checkout the way
checkperf does: with the old name it configures master with -freflection
-std=c++26, with the new one it configures clean. Full suite passes (119/119).

* some cleaning.

* need to allow ==
